newsitem.title: UK: Moody's affirms Koninklijke Eurobond rating.
newsitem.headline: Moody's affirms Koninklijke Eurobond rating.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service Ltd said on Wednesday it confirmed the AA1 rating of Koninklijke PTT Nederland (KPN) NV's 1.3 billion guilder Eurobond.
It also said it placed under review for possible upgrade TNT (USA) Inc and TNT Transport (Europe) Plc's B1 rated $100 million unsecured notes (joint and several obligation of both entities).

Moody's said in a statment the moves follow an announcement earlier on Wednesday that KPN (Australia) Limited had made an offer to acquire all the ordinary shares and converting preference shares of TNT Ltd for approximately A$2.0 billion.
The offer is conditional upon acceptance of at least 90 percent of shareholders and approval of appropriate regulatory bodies, Moody's said.

"Moody's rating of KPN's bond, issued in June of this year, anticipated the likelihood that KPN would pursue an active acquisition strategy focused on accelerating the company's international postal business," it said.

The proposed acquisition of TNT Ltd fits within this strategy, because it will enable PTT Post to significantly expand and improve its position in the international time-sensitive distribution and logistics operations, Moody's said.

"However it does expose KPN to additional operating risks derived from the highly competitive global logistics and time-sensitive businesses, the broad geographical footprint of TNT's operations as well as the nature of its non-core businesses such as its aircraft sales and leasing business and its shipping business in Australia and New Zealand," Moody's said.

"We believe that the size of the investment will not impair KPN's financial stability and that it will contribute to further diversification of KPN's consolidated cash flow base. We also expect no further significant acquisitions to take place in the near future," Moody's said.

"The review of TNT (USA) Inc and TNT Transport (Europe) Plc debt ratings will focus on the ultimate structure of the acquisition, including the likelihood of success and the treatment of the guaranteed debt in the new group," Moody's said.

KPN NV, headquartered in Groningen, The Netherlands, provides postal, local, long distance, international and mobile telecommunications services through its 7.8 million telephone lines. In addition, KPN provides cable television, multimedia, car leasing and security services, Moody's said.
